chapter_title: Concerning the Four Works of the Ambassador

spiritual_reading.full_translation:
First, the Divine brought forth an efflux of its own quality and set it forth in manifest wisdom, so that what had been hidden within could be grasped in a form fit for reception.

Second, by that manifestation, every passage of communication between higher and lower degrees was opened for the needed admission of influx, and afterward those same passages were closed, so that what had entered might remain arranged in order and not be scattered.

Third, from that self-disclosure there proceeded illumination together with liberation, and this proceeding was cleansed of every mixture that would defile or bend it; and this purified illumination surpassed the former kind of illumination that would otherwise have gone forth.

Fourth, through the bringing of a human receptacle into completeness and right arrangement, the Divine made evident its power to convey and operate in the ultimate degree. By means of that prepared completion it brought forth living consciousness, and this consciousness, in full integrity and abundance, spread its shining life over states hostile to good, so that even in resisted regions a perfected presence might be established and active.

paragraph_translations.translation: First, the Divine brought forth an efflux of its own quality and set it forth in manifest wisdom, so that what was within could be seen and received.
paragraph_translations.connection: BEGINS the chapter by establishing the primary act: self-manifestation in receivable form.

paragraph_translations.translation: Second, by that manifestation, every passage of communication between higher and lower degrees was opened for reception at that moment, and afterward those same passages were closed, so that the admitted influx would remain ordered and not be dispersed.
paragraph_translations.connection: DEVELOPS the effect of the manifestation by describing regulated access of influx.
paragraph_translations.notes: The timing emphasis is preserved as a state-bound opening and closing of communication.

paragraph_translations.translation: Third, from that self-disclosure there proceeded illumination together with liberation, and this proceeding was purified from every admixture that could distort it; and this purified illumination surpassed the illumination that would otherwise have been given forth.
paragraph_translations.connection: DEVELOPS by moving from access to the quality of what proceeds—clarified enlightenment and freedom.
paragraph_translations.notes: The final comparison is slightly uncertain in referent—whether it contrasts with a former illumination or with a later one—so it is rendered as a contrast with unpurified proceeding.

paragraph_translations.translation: Fourth, through the completion of a human receptacle in proper order, the Divine made evident its conveyance and operation in the ultimate degree. By means of that prepared receptacle it brought forth living consciousness, and this consciousness, in perfection and fullness, extended its shining life into states opposed to good.
paragraph_translations.connection: DEVELOPS into embodiment in the ultimate degree and the extension of perfected life into hostile states.
paragraph_translations.notes: The phrase about “perfection of people” presses toward the idea of a completed human receptacle; the final domain is rendered as active opposition to good.

spiritual_reading.overall_coherence: The chapter holds together as a compact fourfold sequence: manifestation, opening/closing of regulated influx, purified illumination and liberation, and then embodiment in a completed human receptacle with extension into oppositional states. The voice is consistent and the progression is linear; the only mild stumble is the comparative clause in the third work, whose target of comparison is not fully explicit.

findings.diagnosis: Clean, compact correspondential fourfold teaching with linear progression. No intrusion of administrative (jurisdictional) cataloguing, no named powers, no rank-inventories, and no seam-expansion. The spiritual reading does not report any narrative break; the chapter’s “four works” stay in one didactic mode.
findings.evidence: Text is entirely functional/processual: (1) “his image that he displayed” (manifestation-as-function), (2) “doors of the firmaments… opened… shut” (regulated passage), (3) “light and the releasing… purified” (quality/state of emanation), (4) “made apparent… his light ship… brought forth the living soul… shone forth… over the worlds of enmity” (vehicle + emergence of soul + extension into hostile domain). The stage-3a reading confirms: “The chapter holds together as a compact fourfold sequence… The voice is consistent and the progression is linear.” No mention of alien names or governance terms; the narrative does not require forcing to unify disparate materials.

findings.diagnosis: Genuine local ambiguity in a comparative clause (“more than the light that he shall [give forth]”) due to an unclear referent (what ‘other’ light is being compared). This is not a voice-switch or insertion; it is a normal micro-level textual/semantic difficulty (possibly damage/ellipsis) inside an otherwise coherent correspondential unit.
findings.evidence: The spiritual reading’s only stumble is explicitly confined here: “The final comparison is slightly uncertain in referent… whose target of comparison is not fully explicit.” The Coptic restoration likewise signals uncertainty with brackets: “he shall [give forth]”. Nothing about this clause introduces administrative governance, named authorities, or a taxonomic addendum; it remains within the chapter’s functional theme (purified light/release). Removing it would not improve narrative coherence; it would only delete the intended rhetorical comparison.

textual_criticism.summary: 2 findings total: (1) chapter-wide confirmation of a coherent correspondential substrate (no action), (2) one genuine, local comparative-referent ambiguity at ¶4 (no action). Excision: 0. Annotation: 0. None: 2.

harmonized_paragraphs.text: The first is his image that he displayed in a glorious image.
The second is all the doors of the firmaments that were opened at that time. They open [before him] and shut behind him.
The third is the light and the releasing that was purified by his image. That light is more than the light that he shall [give forth]
The fourth: He has [made apparent], by the perfection of people, his light ship. He has [brought forth] the living soul that shone forth in perfection and fullness over the worlds of enmity.

changes_summary: No changes made. Finding 1 recommends none for ¶2–¶5 (coherent correspondential sequence), and Finding 2 recommends none for ¶4 (local ambiguity not warranting excision).
